message.content:
### Tenant Rights in Texas (as of 2026) | Area | Key Rights | How to Exercise Them | |------|------------|----------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within **30 days** after lease ends, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a copy of the lease and any receipts for repairs.
• Request a written itemized statement of deductions. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must keep the premises in a safe, sanitary condition (plumbing, heating, electrical, etc.).
• Must comply with all building codes and health regulations. | • Report problems in writing (email or certified mail).
• If unresolved, you may file a complaint with the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA) or seek a court order. | | **Rent Increases** | • No statutory limit on how much rent can be increased, but it must be in writing and given **at least 30 days’ notice** for month‑to‑month tenants, **60 days** for longer leases. | • Review your lease for any rent‑increase clauses.
• Negotiate or seek mediation if you believe the increase is unreasonable. | | **Lease Termination** | • Either party may terminate a month‑to‑month lease with **30 days’ written notice**.
• For fixed‑term leases, the landlord must provide a **written notice of termination** at least **30 days** before the lease ends. | • Keep a copy of the notice and any correspondence. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • You have the right to live without unreasonable interference from the landlord or other tenants. | • Document any disturbances and notify the landlord in writing. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major issue, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from rent, but only after giving written notice and allowing a reasonable time for repair. | • Keep receipts and a written notice to the landlord. | | **Fair Housing** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income. | • File a complaint with the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) or the Texas Commission on Human Rights (TCHR). | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must provide a **written notice** (usually 3 days for nonpayment, 30 days for lease violations).
• Eviction must go through the court; landlords cannot forcibly remove you. | • Respond promptly to notices.
• Seek legal counsel or tenant advocacy groups if you receive an eviction notice. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) before entering the unit, except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of any entries and request a written record if you suspect unlawful entry. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide a written statement of utility responsibilities if utilities are not included in rent. | • Verify the statement and keep copies of utility bills. | | **Dispute Resolution** | • Many disputes can be resolved through mediation or small‑claims court (up to $20,000). | • Contact the Texas Small Claims Court or local mediation services. | #### Quick Tips for Protecting Your Rights 1. **Read the Lease Carefully** – Understand all clauses, especially those about rent, repairs, and termination. 2. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of all communications, receipts, and photos of any issues. 3. **Know the Law** – Familiarize yourself with the Texas Property Code (Title 8, Chapter 91) and local ordinances. 4. **Seek Help Early** – Contact tenant advocacy groups (e.g., Texas Tenants Union) or legal aid if you face disputes. 5. **Keep Records of Notices** – If you receive a notice from your landlord, keep a copy and note the date received. --- **Disclaimer:** This information is general in nature and not legal advice. For specific legal questions, consult a licensed attorney or a local tenant advocacy organization.
